questions.prompt: What makes the migration planner deterministic, and why is the plan's hash not enough to make apply safe on its own?

keyPoints.text: Equivalent snapshots must produce the same operations.
keyPoints.quote: A deterministic planner produces the same operations from equivalent snapshots.

keyPoints.text: Ordering is normalized before anything is hashed or compared.
keyPoints.quote: This implementation normalizes ordering before hashing and comparison.

keyPoints.text: Definition types and entry handles are the business identities; field keys identify values inside an entry.
keyPoints.quote: Definition types and entry handles form business identities

keyPoints.text: Duplicate identities are rejected so a later lookup cannot arbitrarily pick one of two records.
keyPoints.quote: a later lookup might arbitrarily select one of two records

keyPoints.text: A hash only detects changed content; it is not authorization or a signature.
keyPoints.quote: it is not authorization or a digital signature

keyPoints.text: Apply re-exports both stores and rebuilds the whole plan before comparing.
keyPoints.quote: It re-exports source and target, rebuilds the entire plan and compares the resulting artifact.

keyPoints.text: The check is a preflight snapshot; another writer can still change the store before a create.
keyPoints.quote: another writer can change the remote store after export and before a create

questions.prompt: Explain the three kinds of success for a mutation and how the tool treats timeouts and retries.

keyPoints.text: An HTTP 200 only means the transport received a response.
keyPoints.quote: An HTTP 200 means the transport received a response.

keyPoints.text: The GraphQL envelope can still carry top-level errors.
keyPoints.quote: The GraphQL envelope may still contain top-level errors.

keyPoints.text: A mutation payload can contain userErrors or lack a created ID.
keyPoints.quote: A mutation payload may also contain `userErrors` or lack a created resource ID.

keyPoints.text: A timeout after sending a mutation leaves the outcome uncertain, since the remote may have committed.
keyPoints.quote: The remote service may have committed even though the client did not receive its ID.

keyPoints.text: Automatic retry could create duplicates or hit an existing handle, so mutation failures stop execution.
keyPoints.quote: Therefore mutation transport failures stop execution and require a fresh export.

keyPoints.text: Read retries are bounded and limited to selected statuses or throttling.
keyPoints.quote: Read retries are bounded and apply only to selected HTTP status codes or explicit GraphQL throttling.

keyPoints.text: Retrying every error would hide validation problems and amplify outages.
keyPoints.quote: Retrying every error would hide validation problems and amplify outages.

questions.prompt: Why does the planner build explicit create inputs instead of copying fetched objects, and how does it handle references, target-only entries and partial failure?

keyPoints.text: The old script mutated the shared source object and assumed every returned field was valid on create.
keyPoints.quote: That both changed the shared source object and assumed every returned field was accepted on create.

keyPoints.text: The new planner constructs explicit inputs.
keyPoints.quote: The new planner constructs explicit inputs.

keyPoints.text: PUBLIC_READ_WRITE admin access is an output-only value, so it is not echoed into the mutation.
keyPoints.quote: is an output value absent from the create-input enum

keyPoints.text: A product ID belongs to its source store, so reference definitions are blocked rather than having fields dropped.
keyPoints.quote: The current planner blocks those definitions rather than dropping reference fields.

keyPoints.text: Target-only entries are reported and retained.
keyPoints.quote: absence from a source export is not enough evidence to delete them

keyPoints.text: The journal records confirmed creates but cannot roll back earlier remote operations.
keyPoints.quote: it cannot roll back earlier remote operations

keyPoints.text: A failed journal write after a real create means reconciliation must still inspect the remote target.
keyPoints.quote: reconciliation must still inspect the remote target
